spec_match.rationale: Right surface and a genuinely good angle (live entry plus a simulated pre-145 DPR² score), but the user-triggered flow is filtered out by its own hadRecentInput check, and the 100ms internal delay in triggerShift() is inside the 500ms recent-input window.

interactive.rationale: CDP-verified: clicking ▶ Trigger shift visibly moves the block, yet the score panels stay '—' and the log says 'No shifts yet' because the resulting entry has hadRecentInput=true and is discarded; worse, unrelated buffered load-time shifts do get logged and are mislabelled 'shift 100px' with the current slider value.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Blurb promises reading the real entry in CSS pixels plus a DPR=2/3 pre-145 simulation — exactly the spec's motivation.

edge_cases.rationale: DPR 1×/2×/3× simulation buttons and a distance slider exist, but the hadRecentInput edge case silently defeats the page and mislabelled buffered entries actively mislead.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/5155103518228480 and all three sibling concepts.

conformance.rationale: Shares the structural feature suite (6/6 here); nothing asserts this page's simulated-score arithmetic.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Real CDP clicks: block shifts, console clean, but the core readout never reflects the triggered shift; the CLI screenshot additionally caught load-time entries logged as 'shift 100px' — evidence of the mislabelling.

telemetry_health.rationale: Server-injected /public/demo-telemetry.js verified in the served DOM.

design_system.rationale: Variables throughout; .trigger-btn overrides background and color together per invariant 6.

accessibility.rationale: The distance slider has an aria-label and DPR buttons are native, but score panels and the entry log update with no live region.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: CDP-measured clean at 360x740 (scrollWidth 360; wide code stays inside scrollable pre); desktop verified via screenshot.

openQuestions.title: Fix the dead readout: trigger the shift outside the hadRecentInput window
openQuestions.detail: triggerShift() mutates marginTop ~0-100ms after the click, so every entry arrives with hadRecentInput=true and `continue` drops it — CDP-verified (block moves, panels stay '—', log stays 'No shifts yet'). Delay the mutation >500ms with a visible countdown, or surface hadRecentInput entries explicitly. Shared defect with cls-demo and zoom-resilience-checker.

openQuestions.title: Stop mislabelling unrelated entries as 'shift Npx'
openQuestions.detail: The log template stamps every observed entry with the current shiftDist ('shift 100px'), including buffered load-time shifts that have nothing to do with the control (seen in the CLI screenshot: five load entries all labelled 'shift 100px', two with prev/curr y=0). Only label entries whose source rect matches the demo element, and mark others as 'page shift'.

summary: The most ambitious of the LayoutShift pages (live value + pre-145 DPR² simulation side-by-side) but its core flow is dead: the click-triggered shift is always discarded as hadRecentInput, and buffered page-load shifts get logged mislabelled as the user's '100px' shift. Layout is clean on both viewports; the fix is a delayed trigger plus source-matched logging. Browser-verified with headless Chromium 141.0.7390.37 via CLI (screenshot + DOM dump) and raw CDP (real click dispatch, console/network capture, 360x740 DPR3 mobile emulation) — chrome-devtools-mcp is unavailable in this cloud session. Chromium 141 predates Chrome 145, so v145-only API paths were validated on their fallback branches, not the new-API success path. The single failed fonts.googleapis.com stylesheet request is environmental (blocked host) and was not counted against any page.
